_skip: Test runs do not install the helper.

Only the %lld sites in your list..one: Only the one site in your list.
Only the %lld sites in your list..other: Only the %lld sites in your list.

_note.Add %lld Sites: Undo menu action name: Edit menu shows 'Undo <this>'. The number is never shown; forms only pick singular/plural.
_note.Delete %lld Sites: Undo menu action name: Edit menu shows 'Undo <this>'. The number is never shown; forms only pick singular/plural.
_note.%@ Copy: Default name for a duplicated strategy; %@ is the original strategy name.
_note.%lld h %@ min: Running time, e.g. '1 h 05 min'. %@ is two-digit minutes. Use your language's usual short units.
_note.%lld min: Running time in a stat tile, short unit.
_note.%lld s: Running time in a stat tile, seconds, short unit.
_note.%lld ms: Milliseconds after a response time, short unit.
_note.Opens · %lld · %lld ms: Result of opening a site: 'opens' · HTTP status code · response time.
_note.Bypass: Menu bar menu title (top of the screen) for the on/off commands. One short word.
_note.Bypass On: Status shown in the sidebar footer and menu bar menu: the bypass is running.
_note.Off: Status shown in the sidebar footer and menu bar menu: the bypass is not running.
_note.On: A small tag in a sample preview row meaning the site is turned on.
_note.Follow: Toolbar toggle in the log: keep scrolling to the newest line.
_note.Show: Label of a segmented filter: All / Sites / Errors. Hidden in the toolbar, read by VoiceOver.
_note.List: Label of the segmented control Sites to Unblock / Never Touch. Read by VoiceOver.
_note.Never Touch: Name of the list of sites the bypass must never change (banks etc.). Short segmented-control label.
_note.Sites to Unblock: Name of the list of sites the bypass should open. Short segmented-control label.
_note.My list: Segmented control next to 'All sites': only sites in the user's list. Very short.
_note.My List: Menu bar picker item, same meaning as 'My list'.
_note.All sites: Segmented control: every site goes through the bypass. Very short.
_note.All Sites: Menu bar picker item, same meaning as 'All sites'.
_note.Use: Small button on a row: start using this strategy.
_note.In use: Small tag on a strategy card: this is the strategy currently used.
_note.Yours: Section title: the strategies the user made.
_note.Built-in: Section title: strategies that ship with the app.
_note.Disorder: tpws option name in a summary line ('Split at 1,midsld · Disorder').
_note.OOB byte: tpws option in a summary line: an out-of-band (urgent) TCP byte.
_note.Split at %@: Summary line; %@ is a technical position like '1,midsld'.
_note.TLS records at %@: Summary line; %@ is a technical position like 'sniext+1'.
_note.Split at: Form field label: where to split the packet; value is like '1,midsld'.
_note.host: lowercase: Toggle: write the HTTP header name 'Host:' in lowercase as 'host:'. Keep 'host:' verbatim.
_note.MiXeD domain case: Toggle: write the domain in mixed upper/lower case. Show the mixed case playfully in your own word if natural.
_note.Line break before method: Toggle: add a line break before the HTTP method (GET/POST).
_note.Extra space after method: Toggle: add a space after the HTTP method (GET/POST).
_note.My Provider: Placeholder example name for a new strategy, e.g. named after an internet provider.
_note.Find a Strategy: Sheet title and toolbar button: tests every strategy on a blocked site.
_note.Check: Button that opens a site with and without the bypass to compare.
_note.Address: Text field label for a website address.
_note.Copy the lines shown. Hold for the tpws: Tooltip on a toolbar button with a menu: click copies the log lines; press and hold shows a menu.
_note.Turn the bypass on (Command-B): Tooltip. Keep the shortcut in parentheses; write it the way Mac menus in your language name the key (Command / Befehl / Comando / Commande...). Same for every '(Command-…)' / '(Shift-Command-…)' tooltip.
_note.Quick: Segmented control in Find a Strategy: try only the built-in and the user's strategies. One short word.
_note.Thorough: Segmented control in Find a Strategy: try blockcheck's whole list (39 tries). One short word.
_note.Scan: Accessibility label of the Quick/Thorough segmented control.
_note.OOB: Short label inside a generated strategy name, e.g. 'Split at 1 · OOB' (out-of-band byte). Keep it very short; OOB may stay as is.
_note.Host case: Short label inside a generated strategy name: the Host header written as 'host'.
_note.Host spelled %@: Short label inside a generated strategy name; %@ is the spelling, e.g. hoSt.
_note.Host padding %@: Short label inside a generated strategy name; %@ is a byte count, e.g. 1024.
_note.%@ strategy: Suggested name for a strategy saved from a scan; %@ is a site, e.g. discord.com.
_note.%@: %@: One site's result in a tooltip: site name, then the reason it failed.
_note.%@: opens in %lld ms: One site's result in a tooltip: site name opened in so many milliseconds.
_note.Opened %lld of %lld: Small text on a result row: how many of the tested sites opened, e.g. 'Opened 2 of 3'.
_note.%lld of %lld tried…: Progress line while strategies are tested, e.g. '12 of 39 tried…'.
Footer after the user pressed Stop: how many tries finished out of all.
_note.Save as Strategy…: Small button on a working result row: open the strategy editor with this row's flags.
_note.Also scan HTTP: Footer button after an HTTPS scan: run the plain-HTTP tries on the same site.
_note.Save HTTP + HTTPS Strategy…: Footer button: save one strategy that uses the best HTTP try for port 80 and the best HTTPS try for port 443.
_note.%@ only works on Linux. On a Mac it does: Orange note in the strategy editor; %@ is a tpws flag like --mss.
_note.Delete %lld Subscriptions: Undo menu action name: Edit menu shows 'Undo <this>'. The number is never shown; forms only pick singular/plural.
_note.Updated %@: Row caption of a subscribed list; %@ is a relative time already in the user's language, e.g. '2 hours ago' / 'vor 2 Stunden'. Write it so that phrase fits.
_note.Space: Name of the Space bar key, shown in a keyboard shortcut like '⌃⌥Space'. Use the key name your macOS uses.
_note.Help: Name of the Help key, shown in a keyboard shortcut. Use the key name your macOS uses.
_note.Add to: Picker label in the Add Subscription sheet: which list the subscription goes to (Sites to Unblock / Never Touch).
_note.From the address: Placeholder of the optional Name field: if empty, the name is taken from the address.
_note.Subscriptions: Section title on the Sites page: lists downloaded from the web.
_note.Subscribe: Default button of the Add Subscription sheet.
_note.Global shortcut: Settings row label: a keyboard shortcut that works in every app.
_note.Shortcut: Settings section title for the global shortcut.
_note.Type Shortcut: Shown inside the shortcut recorder while it waits for keys. Very short.
_note.Record Shortcut: Shown inside the shortcut recorder when no shortcut is set. Very short.
_note.Only the sites in your list go through Z: Caption of the System proxy row when only listed sites use the proxy (PAC mode).
_note.Transparent mode: Name of the mode where every app's web traffic goes through tpws with no proxy settings (pf redirection by a root helper). Section title and row label; pick one natural name and use it in every string that mentions it.
_note.Helper: Row label: the small background program that runs as administrator for Transparent mode. Value is its state (Ready / Not installed / Needs approval in Login Items).
_note.Ready: State of the helper: installed and answering.
_note.Remove the helper?: Title of a confirmation alert before removing the helper.
_note.Turn on ZapretMac in System Settings, un: Use the names your macOS gives these panes (System Settings > General > Login Items & Extensions).
_note.What is Transparent mode?: Title of a small popover opened by a ? button next to 'Transparent mode'. Use the same name for the mode as everywhere else in your file.
_note.Normally ZapretMac works as a proxy: app: Body of the ? popover and its hover tooltip. Readers are everyday users who do not know what a proxy is: keep it short, plain, and friendly; use the same words for 'helper' and the mode as in the rest of your file.
